name: Mirko Ilić
line1: Bosnian-born illustrator and graphic designer based in New York; former art director at Time magazine and The New York Times Op-Ed page.
line2: Known for provocative political illustration, Rage Against the Machine's album art, and the opening titles for You've Got Mail.

name: Tina Roth-Eisenberg
line1: Swiss-born graphic designer based in Brooklyn, New York; founder of the swissmiss design blog and studio.
line2: Known for launching CreativeMornings, the TeuxDeux to-do app, and the temporary-tattoo company Tattly.

name: Walter Herdeg
line1: Swiss graphic designer and publisher based in Zurich; co-founder and longtime editor of Graphis magazine.
line2: Known for founding and editing Graphis for more than four decades, publishing its design annuals, and promoting Swiss poster art abroad.

name: Louis Braille
line1: French educator and inventor based in Paris; blinded in a childhood accident, he taught at the Royal Institute for Blind Youth.
line2: Known for inventing the Braille tactile reading and writing system, adapting it for musical notation, and transforming literacy for the blind.

name: Celestino Piatti
line1: Swiss graphic artist and illustrator; principal designer for the Munich-based dtv paperback publishing house for over three decades.
line2: Known for designing nearly all of dtv's paperback covers and typography, prize-winning Swiss poster art, and the illustrated Vogelbuch.

name: Albert Henry Munsell
line1: American painter and art educator based in Boston; professor at the Massachusetts Normal Art School in the early 1900s.
line2: Known for creating the Munsell color system, founding the Munsell Color Company, and standardizing color notation for science and industry.

name: Charles Addams
line1: American cartoonist based in New York City; longtime contributor to The New Yorker magazine for over five decades.
line2: Known for creating The Addams Family characters, his macabre single-panel cartoons, and inspiring the hit TV series and films.

name: John Baskerville
line1: English printer and typeface designer based in Birmingham; a leading figure of 18th-century fine printing.
line2: Known for creating the Baskerville typeface, pioneering smoother paper and richer ink for sharper printing, and his acclaimed edition of Virgil.

name: Frank Kozik
line1: Spanish-born American illustrator and poster artist based in Austin and San Francisco; pioneer of the designer toy movement.
line2: Known for reviving rock concert poster art in the 1980s-90s, Man's Ruin Records cover art, and designer vinyl toys at Kidrobot.

name: Massimo Vignelli
line1: Italian-born graphic and industrial designer based in New York; co-founder of Vignelli Associates.
line2: Known for the 1972 New York City subway map, the American Airlines logo, and decades of modernist corporate identity work.

name: Pedro Friedeberg
line1: Italian-born Mexican surrealist artist and designer based in Mexico City; trained as an architect before turning to art.
line2: Known for creating the iconic Hand Chair, hallucinatory paintings of imaginary architecture, and blending surrealism with Mexican folk motifs.

name: John Berg
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; longtime art director and creative director at Columbia Records.
line2: Known for designing thousands of album covers, including Bob Dylan's Greatest Hits, Born to Run, and Chicago's evolving logo artwork.

name: Ikko Tanaka
line1: Japanese graphic designer based in Tokyo; a leading figure in postwar Japanese design and a founding member of Nippon Design Center.
line2: Known for his geometric Nihon Buyo poster, branding for Issey Miyake and Muji, and merging traditional Japanese aesthetics with modernism.

name: Richard Felton Outcault
line1: American cartoonist based in New York; drew rival comic strips for Pulitzer's and Hearst's newspapers in the 1890s.
line2: Known for creating The Yellow Kid, widely considered the first newspaper comic strip, and the later strip Buster Brown.

name: Pablo Ferro
line1: Cuban-born American graphic designer and filmmaker based in New York; pioneer of fast-cut title sequence editing.
line2: Known for the title sequences for Dr. Strangelove and Bullitt, and the poster art for A Clockwork Orange.

name: Colin Banks
line1: British graphic designer and typographer based in London; co-founder of the design firm Banks & Miles.
line2: Known for redesigning the London Underground's New Johnston typeface, the British Telecom logo, and Royal Mail's postcode alphabet.

name: Bob Gill
line1: American graphic designer based in London; a founding figure of the design studio that became Pentagram.
line2: Known for witty conceptual posters and book jackets, founding Fletcher/Forbes/Gill, and his influential design manifesto Forget All the Rules.

name: Art Paul
line1: American graphic designer based in Chicago; the founding art director of Playboy magazine from 1953 to 1982.
line2: Known for designing the iconic Playboy Rabbit Head logo, shaping the magazine's visual identity, and championing editorial illustration.

name: Carin Goldberg
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; a pioneer of postmodern style in American book and record cover design.
line2: Known for the album cover for Madonna's Like a Virgin, witty book jackets for major publishers, and teaching at the School of Visual Arts.

name: Al Hirschfeld
line1: American caricaturist based in New York; chronicled Broadway and Hollywood for The New York Times for over 75 years.
line2: Known for his fluid line caricatures of stage and film stars, and for hiding the name "NINA" within his drawings.

name: Alfred Mahlau
line1: German painter and graphic artist based in Lübeck; a leading figure in early 20th-century German commercial art.
line2: Known for the Niederegger marzipan trademark, poster and map designs for the city of Lübeck, and the Marienkirche's Dance of Death window.

name: Gerard Unger
line1: Dutch graphic and type designer based in Bussum; a leading figure in late 20th-century typeface design.
line2: Known for creating the typefaces Demos, Swift, and Gulliver, among the first typefaces made for digital typesetting.

name: Silvano Campeggi
line1: Italian painter and poster artist based in Florence; known professionally as "Nano," he painted for cinema from the 1940s.
line2: Known for Italian release posters for Gone with the Wind, Casablanca, and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

name: Cassandre
line1: French poster artist and typeface designer based in Paris; born in Kharkiv, Ukraine, he became a leading figure of Art Deco graphics.
line2: Known for his Normandie ocean liner poster, the Dubonnet advertising campaign, and typefaces including Bifur and Peignot.

name: Carlo Vergara
line1: Filipino comic book artist and writer based in Manila; also a theater performer and published playwright.
line2: Known for creating the graphic novel character Zsazsa Zaturnnah, adapted into a hit film and musical, and winning two National Book Awards.

name: Barbara Kruger
line1: American conceptual artist based in New York and Los Angeles; began her career as a magazine designer and photo editor.
line2: Known for bold red, white, and black text-and-image works like "I shop therefore I am" and "Your body is a battleground."

name: Ken Sugimori
line1: Japanese illustrator and game designer based in Tokyo; co-founder and chief character designer at Game Freak.
line2: Known for designing the original Pokémon creatures, the franchise's box art, and its enduring visual identity.

name: Suehiro Maruo
line1: Japanese manga artist based in Tokyo; a leading figure of the ero guro (erotic grotesque) movement.
line2: Known for the manga Mr. Arashi's Amazing Freak Show and Panorama of Hell, and a signature style blending beauty with horror.

name: Patrick Caulfield
line1: British painter based in London; studied at the Royal College of Art alongside the Pop Art generation.
line2: Known for flat, bold-outlined still-life and interior paintings, and representing Britain at the 1972 Venice Biennale.

name: Ole Søndergaard
line1: Danish graphic and type designer based in Copenhagen; trained as a sign painter before founding his own studio in 1973.
line2: Known for creating the FF Signa typeface family, corporate identity and signage systems, and decades of teaching design in Copenhagen.

name: Leif Podhajsky
line1: Australian graphic designer and art director based in Berlin; known for a psychedelic, nature-inspired visual style.
line2: Known for album art for Tame Impala's Innerspeaker and Lonerism, and cover artwork for Bonobo and Foals.

name: Lotta Nieminen
line1: Helsinki-born illustrator and graphic designer based in New York; founder of her own multidisciplinary design studio.
line2: Known for her Cook in a Book children's series for Phaidon, the book Walk This World, and branding and illustration for Hermès and Google.

name: José Guadalupe Posada
line1: Mexican printmaker, engraver, and illustrator active in Mexico City; a prolific satirical cartoonist under the Porfirio Díaz regime.
line2: Known for creating La Calavera Catrina, decades of satirical calavera prints, and illustrations for popular broadsides and chapbooks.

name: Dolly Rudeman
line1: Dutch graphic designer and poster artist active in Amsterdam; one of the first women to design film posters in the Netherlands.
line2: Known for her Art Deco poster for Battleship Potemkin, promotional art for Greta Garbo and Charlie Chaplin films, and 1950s advertising work.

name: Shigeo Fukuda
line1: Japanese graphic designer and sculptor based in Tokyo; first Japanese designer inducted into the New York Art Directors Club Hall of Fame.
line2: Known for the anti-war poster Victory 1945, his 1982 Earth Day poster, and the illusion sculpture Lunch with a Helmet On.

name: Susan Kare
line1: American graphic designer based in the San Francisco Bay Area; former creative director at NeXT following her pioneering work at Apple.
line2: Known for designing the original Macintosh icons and typefaces, including Chicago and Geneva, the Happy Mac, and Clarus the Dogcow.

name: Karlgeorg Höfer
line1: German calligrapher and typographer based in Offenbach; longtime professor at the city's design school, the Werkkunstschule/HfG Offenbach.
line2: Known for the typefaces Salto and Zebra, and for designing Germany's forgery-resistant FE-Schrift license-plate font.

name: Walter Diethelm
line1: Swiss graphic designer and typographer based in Zürich; a leading figure in mid-20th-century Swiss type and signage design.
line2: Known for the typeface Diethelm Antiqua, the type design Sculptura, and co-authoring the reference book Signet, Signal, Symbol.

name: Alvin Lustig
line1: American graphic designer and typographer based in Los Angeles and New York; art director for New Directions Books.
line2: Known for modernist book jacket designs for New Directions, including the cover for Lorca's 3 Tragedies, and crossover work in architecture and interior design.

name: Javier Mariscal
line1: Spanish artist and designer born in Valencia, based in Barcelona since 1970; founder of Estudio Mariscal.
line2: Known for creating Cobi, mascot of the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, the 'Bar Cel Ona' logo, and the Duplex stool shown with the Memphis Group.

name: Konrad Klapheck
line1: German painter based in Düsseldorf; longtime professor at the Düsseldorf Art Academy.
line2: Known for precise, surrealist-tinged paintings of machines, including typewriters and sewing machines, used as stand-ins for human psychology.

name: Jock Kinneir
line1: British graphic designer and typographer based in London; headed the Royal College of Art's graphic design department from 1964.
line2: Known for devising Britain's road sign system with Margaret Calvert, including the Transport typeface and the UK's motorway signage, still in use today.

name: Quentin Fiore
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; corporate design consultant for the Ford Foundation, Bell Laboratories, and RCA.
line2: Known for designing The Medium Is the Massage with Marshall McLuhan, War and Peace in the Global Village, and Buckminster Fuller's I Seem to Be a Verb.

name: Henry Steiner
line1: Austrian-born graphic designer based in Hong Kong since 1961; studied under Paul Rand at Yale, dubbed the 'Father of Hong Kong Graphic Design.'
line2: Known for designing the HSBC hexagon logo, Standard Chartered's Hong Kong banknotes, and corporate identity work for the Hong Kong Jockey Club.

name: Nelly Schwabacher
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] German-Jewish graphic artist from Frankfurt, later a refugee in London; worked for the Frankfurter Zeitung newspaper.
line2: Known for illustration at the Frankfurter Zeitung until her 1935 dismissal under Nazi laws; work held by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum.

name: Shepard Fairey
line1: American street artist and graphic designer based in Los Angeles; founder of OBEY Clothing and the Obey Giant art campaign.
line2: Known for the 2008 Barack Obama 'Hope' poster, the OBEY Giant sticker campaign, and murals held in the collections of MoMA and the Smithsonian.

name: Giambattista Bodoni
line1: Italian typographer, type designer, and printer; ran the Duke of Parma's Royal Press (Stamperia Reale) from 1768 until his death in 1813.
line2: Known for the Bodoni typeface, his Manuale Tipografico specimen book, and acclaimed editions of Horace, Virgil, and Homer's Iliad.

name: Daniel Gil Pila
line1: Spanish graphic designer based in Madrid; began at record label Hispavox before leading book design for Alianza Editorial from 1966.
line2: Known for thousands of book covers for Alianza Editorial's 'El Libro de Bolsillo' series, pioneering modular Spanish book design.

name: Duane Michals
line1: American photographer based in New York; trained in graphic design before turning to photography in the late 1950s.
line2: Known for pioneering multi-image photo sequences like 'Chance Meeting' and 'Death Comes to the Old Lady,' and for handwritten text on his prints.

name: Ken Garland
line1: British graphic designer and educator based in London; art editor of Design magazine before founding Ken Garland & Associates in 1962.
line2: Known for writing the 1964 First Things First manifesto, redesigning the CND peace symbol, and authoring Mr Beck's Underground Map.

name: Margo Chase
line1: American graphic designer and typographer based in Los Angeles; founder of Chase Design Group in 1986.
line2: Known for logo design for Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Madonna's Like a Prayer, and album packaging for Cher and Prince.

name: Rafał Olbiński
line1: Polish-born illustrator and painter based in New York; emigrated as a political refugee in 1981 and taught at the School of Visual Arts.
line2: Known for surrealist opera posters for New York City Opera, winning the Prix Savignac in 1994, and works held by MoMA and the Smithsonian.

name: Eric Gill
line1: British sculptor, letter-cutter and typeface designer active in the early 20th century, trained under calligrapher Edward Johnston.
line2: Known for the typefaces Gill Sans and Perpetua, and sculptures including Prospero and Ariel at BBC Broadcasting House.

name: Woody Pirtle
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; longtime partner at Pentagram known for witty, economical logos and posters.
line2: Known for the Fine Line Features logo, Amnesty International awareness posters, and winning the 2003 AIGA Medal.

name: Eduardo Lima
line1: Brazilian graphic artist based in London; co-founder of the design studio MinaLima, trained in visual communications in Rio de Janeiro.
line2: Known for the graphic design and prop art of the Harry Potter and Fantastic Beasts films, including the Daily Prophet and Marauder's Map.

name: Pierre Bernard
line1: French graphic designer based in Paris; co-founder of the politically engaged design collective Grapus in 1970.
line2: Known for Grapus's protest and cultural posters, the visual identity of the Louvre, and founding the Atelier de Création Graphique.

name: Oldřich Kulhánek
line1: Czech painter and graphic designer based in Prague; trained at the Academy of Arts under Karel Svolinský.
line2: Known for designing the current Czech banknotes and postage stamps, and for politically charged allegorical drawings and posters.

name: Jony Ive
line1: British industrial designer based in California; former Chief Design Officer at Apple before founding the studio LoveFrom.
line2: Known for designing the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, and for shaping Apple's hardware and software design language.

name: Storm Thorgerson
line1: British graphic designer and filmmaker based in London; co-founder of the design group Hipgnosis.
line2: Known for Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon and Animals album covers, and sleeve art for Led Zeppelin and Genesis.

name: Warren Dayton
line1: American illustrator and graphic designer trained at Chouinard Art Institute; pioneer of 1960s psychedelic poster art in California.
line2: Known for pioneering wearable T-shirt art in 1967, corporate branding work, and founding the Artifact, Ink design studio.

name: Liz McQuiston
line1: British graphic design historian and design practitioner based in London; longtime design lecturer and writer.
line2: Known for the books Suffragettes to She-Devils and Graphic Agitation, chronicling women's and protest graphic design.

name: Arnold Newman
line1: American photographer born in New York; pioneer of 'environmental portraiture' working mid-20th century.
line2: Known for portraits of Igor Stravinsky and Pablo Picasso, and photographing industrialists within their own settings.

name: David A. Carter
line1: American author, illustrator, and paper engineer based in California; former designer at Intervisual Communications.
line2: Known for the bestselling Bugs pop-up book series, One Red Dot, and the Meggendorfer Prize-winning Elements of Pop-Up.

name: Jean-Philippe Lenclos
line1: French designer-colorist based in Paris; founder of the color research studio Atelier 3D Couleur.
line2: Known for developing the 'Geography of Color' method, the book Colors of the World, and his Colors of France study.

name: Elaine Lustig Cohen
line1: American graphic designer and artist based in New York; took over husband Alvin Lustig's studio after his death in 1955.
line2: Known for modernist book covers for Meridian Books and New Directions, architectural signage, and a 2011 AIGA Medal.

name: Piet Mondrian
line1: Dutch painter based in Paris and later New York; co-founder of the De Stijl art movement and Neoplasticism.
line2: Known for grid-based abstract paintings in primary colors, Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow, and Broadway Boogie Woogie.

name: Frederic Goudy
line1: American type designer and printer based in New York; founder of the Village Press.
line2: Known for designing over 100 typefaces including Goudy Old Style, Copperplate Gothic, and Kennerley.

name: Manabu Sakamoto
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Japanese graphic designer and art director working in Tokyo.
line2: Known for corporate identity, poster, and editorial design work for Japanese clients and design organizations.

name: Edward Bawden
line1: English illustrator, printmaker, and official war artist based in Essex; trained at the Royal College of Art.
line2: Known for the linocut series Nine London Monuments, war art documenting Dunkirk and North Africa, and Shell poster ads.

name: Wanda Gág
line1: American children's book author and illustrator born in Minnesota; leading figure of 1920s-30s picture books.
line2: Known for writing and illustrating Millions of Cats, The ABC Bunny, and Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

name: Carolina Laudon
line1: Swedish typographer and graphic designer based in Gothenburg; founder of the studio Laudon Design.
line2: Known for corporate typefaces for Systembolaget and Länsförsäkringar, winning the Berling Prize, and serving as ATypI president.

name: Ethel Reed
line1: American poster artist based in Boston; largely self-taught illustrator active in the 1890s Art Nouveau poster boom.
line2: Known for her 1895 Boston Sunday Herald poster debut, bold botanical poster designs, and acclaim on both sides of the Atlantic.

name: Jean Jullien
line1: French illustrator and graphic artist based in Paris and London; known for minimalist line-based visual humor.
line2: Known for the Peace for Paris symbol, the Playtime picture books, and witty illustrations for The New Yorker and others.

name: Lucian Bernhard
line1: German-born poster designer and typographer who later worked in New York; pioneer of the 'Sachplakat' object-poster style.
line2: Known for the iconic Priester Matches poster, the Bernhard Gothic typeface, and prolific advertising and packaging design.

name: Dominique Stroobant
line1: Belgian-born sculptor, photographer, and graphic artist based in Carrara, Italy since 1970.
line2: Known for sculpture collaborations with Max Bill, co-founding the Floating Stones Group, and pioneering pinhole photography.

name: Herb Lubalin
line1: American graphic designer and typographer based in New York; co-founder of the International Typeface Corporation.
line2: Known for art directing Avant Garde magazine, designing its ligature-heavy logo, and the Avant Garde Gothic typeface.

name: Drew Struzan
line1: American illustrator based in Los Angeles; renowned painter of movie poster key art from the 1970s through 2000s.
line2: Known for iconic posters for the Star Wars saga, the Indiana Jones films, and Back to the Future.

name: Josef Albers
line1: German-born artist and educator based in the United States; former Bauhaus master and chair of Yale's design department.
line2: Known for the Homage to the Square painting series, the book Interaction of Color, and influential color theory teaching.

name: Hans Neuburg
line1: Swiss graphic designer based in Zürich; key figure in developing the International Typographic Style (Swiss Style).
line2: Known for co-founding the journal Neue Grafik, running his own Zürich advertising studio, and leading Icograda.

name: Michael Manwaring
line1: American graphic designer based in San Francisco, later Portland; founder of The Office of Michael Manwaring.
line2: Known for pioneering the postmodern 'Pacific Wave' design movement, Embarcadero Promenade signage, and SFMOMA exhibitions.

name: April Greiman
line1: American graphic designer based in Los Angeles; pioneer of California New Wave and early digital design.
line2: Known for her 'Does It Make Sense?' poster, pioneering Macintosh-made hybrid imagery and type, and leading CalArts design.

name: Norman Ives
line1: American graphic designer and artist based in New Haven; founding faculty member of Yale's graphic design program.
line2: Known for fragmented letterform collages, corporate logos for Knoll International, and the book Eight Symbols.

name: William Morris
line1: English textile designer and writer based in London; founder of the Arts and Crafts movement and Kelmscott Press.
line2: Known for iconic wallpaper and textile patterns, the Morris & Co. design firm, and the illuminated Kelmscott Chaucer.

name: Bradbury Thompson
line1: American graphic designer and art director based in New York; longtime designer of the Westvaco Inspirations series.
line2: Known for art directing Mademoiselle and Smithsonian magazines, the Washburn College Bible, and U.S. postage stamp design.

name: Jacques Nathan-Garamond
line1: French graphic designer based in Paris; founding member of the Alliance Graphique Internationale (AGI).
line2: Known for his 1949 UNESCO human rights poster, Air France advertising campaigns, and Shell's French Cartoguide road maps.

name: Edward Steichen
line1: Luxembourg-born American photographer based in New York; former chief photographer at Condé Nast and MoMA photography curator.
line2: Known for curating the Family of Man exhibition, iconic Vanity Fair celebrity portraits, and pioneering fashion photography.

name: Philip Gips
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; co-founder of the design firm Frankfurt Gips Balkind.
line2: Known for designing the ESPN and History Channel logos, and movie posters for Alien and Rosemary's Baby.

name: Peter Biľak
line1: Slovak-born type and graphic designer based in The Hague; founder of the Typotheque type foundry in 1999.
line2: Known for the Fedra typeface family, pioneering webfonts in 2009, and co-founding the Indian Type Foundry.

name: Koloman Moser
line1: Austrian painter and designer based in Vienna; co-founder of the Vienna Secession and Wiener Werkstätte.
line2: Known for stained glass and graphics for the Secession, Wiener Werkstätte furniture and jewelry, and postage stamp design.

name: Jean Widmer
line1: Swiss-born graphic designer based in Paris; longtime visual identity designer for major French cultural institutions.
line2: Known for the Centre Pompidou logo, the Musée d'Orsay identity, and France's first highway signage system.

name: Jim Rimmer
line1: Canadian letterpress printer and type designer based in New Westminster, British Columbia, who ran the private Pie Tree Press.
line2: Known for hand-cut metal typefaces including Juliana, Albertan, and Stern, and for his memoir Pie Tree Press.

name: Jan Tschichold
line1: German-born typographer and book designer who championed modernist New Typography before settling in Switzerland.
line2: Known for the manifesto Die Neue Typographie, standardizing Penguin Books' postwar design, and the typeface Sabon.

name: Henry van de Velde
line1: Belgian architect, painter, and designer based in Germany, a leading figure of European Art Nouveau.
line2: Known for founding the Weimar arts and crafts school that preceded the Bauhaus, Art Nouveau interiors, and total-design theory.

name: Jessica Hische
line1: American lettering artist, illustrator, and type designer based in the San Francisco Bay Area.
line2: Known for the viral Daily Drop Cap project, the Should I Work for Free? flowchart, and bestselling typographic picture books.

name: Herbert Bayer
line1: Austrian-born graphic designer, painter, and architect; a Bauhaus master who later worked in the United States.
line2: Known for the geometric Universal typeface, Bauhaus exhibition design, and corporate identity work for Container Corporation of America.

name: Yusaku Kamekura
line1: Japanese graphic designer based in Tokyo, a founding figure of postwar Japanese design and co-founder of Nippon Design Center.
line2: Known for the iconic 1964 Tokyo Olympics poster, Expo '70 graphics, and the NTT corporate logo.

name: Erik Bruun
line1: Finnish graphic designer based in Helsinki, trained at the Central School of Industrial Design.
line2: Known for designing Finland's 1986 markka banknotes, the Hartwall Jaffa soft-drink branding, and the Finnish nature conservation logo.

name: Jeremy Fish
line1: American illustrator and fine artist based in San Francisco's North Beach neighborhood.
line2: Known for album art for Aesop Rock, the bronze Haight Street Bunny public sculpture, and skate graphics for Thrasher and DLX.

name: Victor Vasarely
line1: Hungarian-born French painter and graphic artist, widely regarded as a founder of the Op Art movement.
line2: Known for geometric optical-illusion paintings, the Vasarely Museum in Aix-en-Provence, and early kinetic-art experiments.

name: Jukka Veistola
line1: Finnish graphic designer and poster artist based in Helsinki, trained at the Ateneum Art School.
line2: Known for the award-winning poster Yellow Flowers, Warsaw Poster Biennale honors, and posters held in MoMA's permanent collection.

name: Dale Messick
line1: American cartoonist based in Chicago and New York, a pioneer among women in newspaper syndication.
line2: Known for creating Brenda Starr, Reporter in 1940, and receiving the National Cartoonists Society's Milton Caniff Lifetime Achievement Award.

name: Louise Fili
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; former art director of Pantheon Books before founding her own studio.
line2: Known for Italian-inspired restaurant and food packaging identities, including Tate's Bake Shop, and hundreds of book jackets.

name: Oswald Bruce Cooper
line1: American lettering artist and type designer based in Chicago, active in advertising design in the early 20th century.
line2: Known for designing the Cooper Oldstyle and Cooper Black typefaces and co-founding the lettering studio Bertsch & Cooper.

name: Peter Behrens
line1: German architect and designer based in Berlin, a pioneer of modern industrial design and corporate identity.
line2: Known for his comprehensive AEG branding program and for mentoring Walter Gropius, Mies van der Rohe, and Le Corbusier.

name: Jurriaan Schrofer
line1: Dutch graphic designer, typographer, and educator based in Amsterdam, active from the 1950s through the 1980s.
line2: Known for pioneering the Dutch industrial photo book, experimental mathematically inspired typefaces, and the Hoogovens logo.

name: John Halas
line1: Hungarian-born animator and producer based in London; co-founder of the Halas and Batchelor studio.
line2: Known for directing Animal Farm, Britain's first feature-length animated film, and decades of wartime and experimental animation.

name: Ayano Koshiro
line1: Japanese graphic artist and illustrator based in Japan, co-founder of the game studio Ancient.
line2: Known for monster and character designs for Ys, art direction on Streets of Rage 2, and artwork for Sonic the Hedgehog.

name: Felix Hoffmann
line1: Swiss illustrator, graphic designer, and stained-glass artist based in Aarau, Switzerland.
line2: Known for illustrating Brothers Grimm fairy tales, the award-winning A Boy Went Out to Gather Pears, and windows at Bern Minster.

name: John Langdon
line1: American typographer and graphic designer based in Philadelphia, a pioneer of modern ambigram design.
line2: Known for the ambigrams in Dan Brown's Angels & Demons, the Da Vinci Code film's bank logo, and the book Wordplay.

name: Joan Miro
line1: Catalan Spanish painter, sculptor, and ceramicist based in Barcelona and Mallorca, a major figure of Surrealism.
line2: Known for dreamlike biomorphic paintings, the sculpture Woman and Bird in Barcelona, and ceramic murals made with Josep Llorens Artigas.

name: Dieter Roth
line1: German-born Swiss artist who worked across Switzerland, Iceland, and Germany, known for experimental book art.
line2: Known for artist's books made with perishable materials, chocolate and food sculptures, and the collaborative Flat Waste archive.

name: Kurt Wiese
line1: German-born illustrator based in the United States after years spent in China; illustrated several hundred children's books.
line2: Known for illustrating The Story about Ping, the Freddy the Pig series, and the Newbery Medal-winning Young Fu of the Upper Yangtze.

name: Neville Brody
line1: British graphic designer and typographer based in London, former art director of The Face magazine.
line2: Known for radical 1980s magazine design, founding the typeface foundry FontFont, and co-founding the Fuse type journal.

name: Lou Dorfsman
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; longtime creative director and design chief at CBS.
line2: Known for safeguarding the CBS Eye logo, the proprietary CBS Didot typeface, and the Gastrotypographicalassemblage wall at CBS headquarters.

name: Herbert Matter
line1: Swiss-born photographer and graphic designer based in New York; longtime design consultant for Knoll furniture.
line2: Known for pioneering photomontage in 1930s Swiss tourism posters, Knoll's advertising identity, and teaching design at Yale.

name: George Auriol
line1: French graphic artist, poet, and type designer based in Paris, associated with the cabaret Le Chat Noir.
line2: Known for designing the Art Nouveau Auriol typeface still used in Paris Metro signage, and for Chat Noir posters and songs.

name: Tadeusz Gajl
line1: Polish graphic designer and illustrator, born in Vilnius and based in Bialystok, Poland.
line2: Known for his contemporary illustrations of Polish-Lithuanian szlachta coats of arms and the reference book Herbarz polski.

name: Romans Suta
line1: Latvian painter, graphic artist, and stage designer based in Riga, a leading figure of Latvian modernism.
line2: Known for introducing Cubist and Constructivist ideas to Latvia, founding the Baltars porcelain workshop, and designing stage sets.

name: Klaus Voormann
line1: German-born artist and musician based in Hamburg and London, a close friend of the Beatles from their early days.
line2: Known for designing the Grammy-winning cover of the Beatles' Revolver, playing bass with Manfred Mann, and the Bee Gees' Idea cover.

name: Bill Plympton
line1: American animator, cartoonist, and filmmaker based in New York, known for hand-drawn independent animation.
line2: Known for the Oscar-nominated shorts Your Face and Guard Dog, and the fully hand-drawn feature film The Tune.

name: Alexey Brodovitch
line1: Russian-born graphic designer and photographer based in New York; longtime art director of Harper's Bazaar magazine.
line2: Known for bold bleed-photography layouts at Harper's Bazaar, mentoring Richard Avedon and Irving Penn, and his Design Laboratory workshop.

name: Satyajit Ray
line1: Indian filmmaker and graphic designer based in Calcutta; began his career as a book-jacket designer and illustrator at Signet Press.
line2: Known for designing the Ray Roman and Ray Bizarre typefaces, illustrating his own book covers, and redesigning Pather Panchali's jacket.

name: Carl Fischer
line1: American photographer and art director based in New York; longtime collaborator with Esquire magazine's George Lois.
line2: Known for Esquire's iconic 1968 Muhammad Ali 'St. Sebastian' cover and the 1969 Andy Warhol 'drowning in soup' cover.

name: Keith Haring
line1: American artist and illustrator based in New York; rose to fame drawing in the city's subway stations in the early 1980s.
line2: Known for his bold graphic line work, the Radiant Baby icon, and murals and public art promoting social and political causes.

name: Irakli Gamrekeli
line1: Georgian scenographer and graphic artist based in Tbilisi; pioneer of Georgian avant-garde stage design at the Rustaveli Theatre.
line2: Known for his expressionist and constructivist set designs, over 50 theatrical productions, and art direction on the film My Grandmother.

name: Theo Barten
line1: Dutch illustrator and information designer based in the Netherlands; pioneer of computer-aided data visualization from the late 1970s.
line2: Known for winning the 2000 Infographics Annual Award, his detailed editorial infographics, and the illustrated Basic Lines book series.

name: Edwin Land
line1: American scientist and inventor based in Cambridge, Massachusetts; co-founder and longtime president of Polaroid Corporation.
line2: Known for inventing instant photography, the Polaroid Land Camera, and early synthetic polarizing filters.

name: Saul Bass
line1: American graphic designer and filmmaker based in Los Angeles; among the most influential corporate-logo and title designers of the 20th century.
line2: Known for the opening titles of Vertigo and Psycho, the AT&T and United Airlines logos, and the poster for The Man with the Golden Arm.

name: Josef Müller-Brockmann
line1: Swiss graphic designer and teacher based in Zurich; leading figure of the International Typographic (Swiss) Style.
line2: Known for his grid-based concert posters for the Zurich Tonhalle, the book Grid Systems in Graphic Design, and co-founding Neue Grafik magazine.

name: Arnaud Mercier
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] French graphic and interaction designer based in Paris; pioneer of early 2000s digital interface and web design.
line2: Known for designing the Slash culture magazine's website, Ora-Ito's online identity, and influential interactive portfolio work.

name: Salvador Dalí
line1: Spanish surrealist painter and designer based in Catalonia; one of the most prominent artists of the 20th-century avant-garde.
line2: Known for The Persistence of Memory, his collaborations with Alfred Hitchcock and Walt Disney, and the Chupa Chups logo design.

name: Francis Meynell
line1: British typographer and publisher based in London; founder of the Nonesuch Press in 1922.
line2: Known for founding the Nonesuch Press, elevating British book design with modern classical typography, and his influential advertising work at Mather & Crowther.

name: Otl Aicher
line1: German graphic designer and typographer based in Ulm; co-founder of the Ulm School of Design (Hochschule für Gestaltung).
line2: Known for the pictogram system and visual identity for the 1972 Munich Olympics, Lufthansa's corporate identity, and the Rotis typeface.

name: Bruce Rogers
line1: American typographer and book designer based in New England and New York; one of the most celebrated figures in 20th-century fine printing.
line2: Known for designing the Centaur typeface, the Oxford Lectern Bible, and hundreds of elegantly crafted limited-edition books.

name: Marcello Morandini
line1: Italian artist and designer based in Varese; leading figure in geometric and kinetic abstraction since the 1960s.
line2: Known for his black-and-white op-art reliefs and sculptures, architectural facade designs, and museum exhibition design work.

name: S. Neil Fujita
line1: Japanese-American graphic designer based in New York; art director at Columbia Records starting in 1954.
line2: Known for the Dave Brubeck Time Out album cover, the original book jacket for The Godfather, and album art for Charles Mingus and Miles Davis.

name: Arild Kristo
line1: Norwegian photographer and graphic designer based in Oslo; trained at the ArtCenter College of Design in California.
line2: Known for his influential 1960s art photography, co-founding the Manité picture agency, and work spanning film and advertising design.

name: Walter Gropius
line1: German-American architect and designer based in Weimar, then later Massachusetts; founder of the Bauhaus school.
line2: Known for founding the Bauhaus in 1919, pioneering modernist functional design, and designing the Gropius House and Pan Am Building.

name: Ralph Reese
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] American comic book illustrator based in New York; contributed art for Marvel, DC, and syndicated newspaper strips.
line2: Known for his National Lampoon feature One Year Affair with Byron Preiss, drawing the Flash Gordon newspaper strip, and horror comics for Warren.

name: Betty Willis
line1: American graphic designer based in Las Vegas; worked for the Western Neon sign company in the 1950s and 1960s.
line2: Known for designing the iconic 'Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas' sign, which she never copyrighted and gave as a gift to the city.

name: Vittorio Zecchin
line1: Italian painter and glass designer based in Murano; artistic director of the Cappellin-Venini glassworks in the 1920s.
line2: Known for reviving classical Venetian glassmaking forms, designing the iconic Veronese vase, and later directing the M.V.M. Cappellin firm.

name: Aaron Marcus
line1: American graphic designer based in Berkeley, California; pioneer of computer graphics and user-interface design since the 1960s.
line2: Known for founding Aaron Marcus and Associates, pioneering human-computer interaction design, and advancing information visualization standards.

name: Henry Wolf
line1: Austrian-born art director and photographer based in New York; former art director of Esquire, Harper's Bazaar, and Show magazines.
line2: Known for his surreal, minimalist magazine covers, pioneering conceptual photography in editorial design, and founding Henry Wolf Productions.

name: Alexander Girard
line1: American architect and designer based in Santa Fe, New Mexico; head of Herman Miller's textile division from 1952.
line2: Known for his vibrant textile and furniture designs, Braniff International's colorful airline identity, and the restaurant La Fonda del Sol.

name: Tom Phillips
line1: British artist and portraitist based in London; elected Royal Academician known across painting, printmaking, and book art.
line2: Known for A Humument, his decades-long altered-book art project, and portraits of cultural figures for London's National Portrait Gallery.

name: Deborah Sussman
line1: American graphic designer based in Los Angeles; pioneer of environmental graphic design and co-founder of Sussman/Prejza.
line2: Known for the colorful visual identity of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, Euro Disney's signage, and branding for American cities.

name: Daniel Bombardier
line1: Canadian street artist based in Windsor, Ontario; works under the alias Denial since the late 1990s.
line2: Known for his satirical stencil and spray-paint murals on consumerism and politics, a guerrilla sticker campaign, and founding Free 4 All Walls.

name: Piet Zwart
line1: Dutch graphic designer and architect based in Rotterdam; a pioneering modernist known as 'the typotekt'.
line2: Known for his dynamic New Typography advertising for NKF cables and PTT, experimental photomontage, and influential industrial product catalogs.

name: David Lance Goines
line1: American artist and printer based in Berkeley, California; longtime proprietor of the Saint Hieronymus Press.
line2: Known for his bold Art Nouveau-inspired posters, decades of artwork for Chez Panisse restaurant, and limited-edition letterpress books.

name: Erik Spiekermann
line1: German typographer and type designer based in Berlin; founder of the design studio MetaDesign and FontShop.
line2: Known for designing the FF Meta and ITC Officina typefaces, Deutsche Bahn's corporate identity, and the Berlin transit typeface.

name: John Gorham
line1: British graphic designer based in London; freelance designer across typography, packaging, and posters for four decades.
line2: Known for his symmetrical English Riviera tourism poster, British postage stamp designs, and receiving D&AD's President's Award in 1993.

name: Alice Cordelia Morse
line1: American book-cover and stained-glass designer based in New York; trained in Louis Comfort Tiffany's glass studio before turning to publishing.
line2: Known for ornate gilt book covers for major New York publishers, her design for Paul Laurence Dunbar's Lyrics of Lowly Life, and Tiffany stained-glass windows.

name: Bruce Blackburn
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; partner in the design firm Danne & Blackburn.
line2: Known for NASA's 1975 'worm' logotype designed with Richard Danne, and the official symbol for the American Revolution Bicentennial.

name: Mikhail Larionov
line1: Russian-born painter and stage designer who later settled in Paris; co-founder of Rayonism, one of Russia's first abstract art movements.
line2: Known for pioneering Rayonist paintings, stage and costume designs for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes, and his lifelong partnership with Natalia Goncharova.

name: Harry Beck
line1: British engineering draftsman and graphic designer based in London; worked for the London Underground Signals Office.
line2: Known for designing the 1931 London Underground schematic map, whose circuit-diagram layout became the template for transit maps worldwide.

name: Peter Knapp
line1: Swiss-born photographer and art director based in Paris; longtime art director of the French magazine Elle.
line2: Known for reinventing Elle's layout with bold diagonals in the 1960s-70s, directing the TV show Dim Dam Dom, and his fashion photography.

name: Ivan Chermayeff
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; co-founder of the design firm Chermayeff & Geismar.
line2: Known for the Chase Manhattan Bank octagon logo, the Mobil Oil logotype, and the Smithsonian Institution's sunburst symbol.

name: Charles Rennie Mackintosh
line1: Scottish architect and designer based in Glasgow; leading figure of the Glasgow Style and Art Nouveau movement.
line2: Known for designing the Glasgow School of Art, the Hill House in Helensburgh, and his distinctive high-backed 'Mackintosh' chairs.

name: Barry Zaid
line1: Canadian-born illustrator and graphic designer based in New York and London; leading figure in the 1970s Art Deco revival.
line2: Known for the cover of The Beatles' First, a Society of Illustrators Gold Medal, and hundreds of logos and packages including Celestial Seasonings.

name: Sumner Stone
line1: American type designer based in California; served as Adobe Systems' first Director of Typography.
line2: Known for creating the ITC Stone typeface family, leading Adobe's Originals typography program, and later founding Stone Type Foundry.

name: Henryk Tomaszewski
line1: Polish graphic artist based in Warsaw; founder of the influential Polish Poster School.
line2: Known for minimalist, symbol-driven theater and film posters, decades of teaching at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts, and shaping postwar Polish design.

name: Julia Margaret Cameron
line1: British photographer working on the Isle of Wight; pioneer of soft-focus portraiture in the Victorian era.
line2: Known for her intimate close-up portraits of Alfred Tennyson, Charles Darwin, and Thomas Carlyle, and for shaping early fine-art photography.

name: Clarence P. Hornung
line1: American graphic designer and illustrator based in New York; trademark specialist nicknamed 'the Audubon of the Automobile.'
line2: Known for his 1930 book Trade-Marks Designed by Clarence P. Hornung, the Handbook of Designs and Devices, and detailed vintage-automobile illustrations.

name: Carol Twombly
line1: American type designer based in California; worked as a type director at Adobe Systems.
line2: Known for designing the typefaces Trajan, Lithos, and Adobe Caslon.

name: Martin K. Speckter
line1: American advertising executive based in New York; head of his own ad agency and editor of the typography magazine TYPEtalks.
line2: Known for proposing the interrobang punctuation mark in 1962 to combine the question mark and exclamation point into one character.

name: Saul Steinberg
line1: Romanian-born illustrator and cartoonist based in New York; longtime contributor to The New Yorker.
line2: Known for the iconic 'View of the World from 9th Avenue' cover, decades of satirical drawings, and a singular line-drawing style.

name: Gisèle Lagacé
line1: Canadian comic book artist and writer based in Ontario; trained in graphic design at La Cité collégiale.
line2: Known for the long-running webcomic Ménage à 3, Archie Comics work including Archie Meets Ramones, and the Image series Exorsisters.

name: M.C. Escher
line1: Dutch graphic artist based in the Netherlands; renowned for mathematically inspired prints exploring impossible structures and infinity.
line2: Known for the lithographs Relativity and Ascending and Descending, and tessellated, optical-illusion works like Sky and Water.

name: Anton Stankowski
line1: German graphic designer and photographer based in Stuttgart; pioneer of concrete and constructive design.
line2: Known for designing the Deutsche Bank logo, decades of German corporate identity work, and experimental photomontage.

name: W.A. Dwiggins
line1: American book and type designer based in Massachusetts; credited with coining the term 'graphic designer.'
line2: Known for designing the typeface Metro, hundreds of Alfred A. Knopf book designs, and his Marionette Theatre puppet productions.

name: Mike Winkelmann (Beeple)
line1: American digital artist based in South Carolina; creator of the long-running 'Everydays' daily-image project.
line2: Known for the NFT artwork Everydays: The First 5000 Days, which sold at Christie's for $69 million, and large-scale digital installations.

name: Michael Manwaring
line1: American graphic designer based in San Francisco and later Portland; founding figure of the Bay Area's postmodern 'Pacific Wave' design movement.
line2: Known for environmental graphics on San Francisco's Embarcadero Promenade, HP Pavilion signage, and decades leading The Office of Michael Manwaring.

name: Gordon House
line1: British painter and graphic designer based in London; freelance designer for galleries, industry and music labels from 1961.
line2: Known for designing the back cover of the Beatles' White Album, Wings' debut album cover, and co-founding the White Ink print studio.

name: Cipe Pineles
line1: Austrian-born graphic designer based in New York; first woman elected to the Art Directors Club and first female art director at Condé Nast.
line2: Known for art directing Glamour, Seventeen, and Charm magazines, pioneering the use of fine artists for editorial illustration.

name: Hiroshi Ono (Mr. Dotman)
line1: Japanese graphic designer and pixel artist based in Tokyo; longtime Namco artist known by the nickname 'Mr. Dotman.'
line2: Known for the sprite and cabinet art of arcade classics Dig Dug, Xevious, and Galaga, and decades of pioneering pixel-art design.

name: Rudy VanderLans
line1: Dutch-born graphic designer based in Berkeley, California; co-founder of Emigre magazine and type foundry.
line2: Known for art directing Emigre's experimental digital-type design, co-creating typefaces for the foundry, and shaping 1980s-90s digital typography.

name: Milton Glaser
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; co-founder of Push Pin Studios and founder of Milton Glaser, Inc.
line2: Known for the 'I Love NY' logo, his psychedelic 1966 Bob Dylan poster, and decades of magazine and brand identity design.

name: Tadanori Yokoo
line1: Japanese graphic designer and artist based in Tokyo; dubbed 'the Japanese Andy Warhol' for his crossover into fine art.
line2: Known for psychedelic 1960s posters for avant-garde theater, album art for artists like Santana, and a prolific painting career.

name: Hervé Tullet
line1: French author and illustrator based in Paris; creator of playful, interactive children's books.
line2: Known for the bestselling Press Here (Un Livre) series, his 'Ideal Exhibition' art workshops for kids, and over 100 illustrated books.

name: Armin Hofmann
line1: Swiss graphic designer based in Basel; pioneer of the Swiss International Style and longtime co-director of the Basel School of Design.
line2: Known for his iconic 1959 Giselle ballet poster, stark black-and-white typographic work, and training generations of designers in Basel.

name: Leopoldo Méndez
line1: Mexican printmaker and engraver based in Mexico City; founder and leading figure of the Taller de Gráfica Popular collective.
line2: Known for politically charged woodcuts and linocuts supporting agrarian reform, decades of activist printmaking, and influencing Mexican graphic art.

name: Adrian Wilson
line1: American book designer, printer, and typographer based in San Francisco; received a MacArthur Fellowship in 1983.
line2: Known for The Design of Books, printing fine editions for The Limited Editions Club, and chronicling the Nuremberg Chronicle.

name: André Saraiva
line1: Swedish-born French street artist and designer based in Paris; creator of the top-hatted "Mr. A" graffiti tag.
line2: Known for founding the Le Baron nightclubs, designing Hôtel Amour in Paris, and collaborations with Louis Vuitton and Chanel.

name: Sándor Bortnyik
line1: Hungarian avant-garde painter and graphic designer; founder of the Műhely school, Budapest's answer to the Bauhaus.
line2: Known for Constructivist "picture-architecture" paintings, modernist poster design, and mentoring Victor Vasarely.

name: Reid Miles
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; in-house art director for Blue Note Records through the late 1950s and '60s.
line2: Known for defining Blue Note's jazz album covers through bold typography, asymmetric layouts, and tinted session photography.

name: Shel Dorf
line1: American comic-strip letterer and fan organizer based in San Diego; founding force behind San Diego Comic-Con.
line2: Known for co-founding Comic-Con International in 1970, chairing its early organizing committee, and lettering the Steve Canyon strip.

name: Tibor Kalman
line1: Hungarian-born graphic designer based in New York; founder of the influential design firm M&Co.
line2: Known for founding M&Co's irreverent design work, editing Benetton's Colors magazine, and the identity for Restaurant Florent.

name: Guy Billout
line1: French-born illustrator based in New York; longtime contributor to The Atlantic, The New Yorker, and Time.
line2: Known for surreal, deadpan editorial illustrations, the wordless book Something's Not Quite Right, and a 1989 Hamilton King Award.

name: Alan Aldridge
line1: British illustrator and art director based in London; art director for Penguin Books' paperback covers in the 1960s.
line2: Known for The Beatles Illustrated Lyrics, The Butterfly Ball and the Grasshopper's Feast, and psychedelic 1960s poster art.

name: Roy Kuhlman
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; freelance cover designer for Grove Press from the 1950s through the '60s.
line2: Known for roughly 700 Grove Press book jackets, bringing Abstract Expressionism into mass-market publishing design.

name: Will H. Bradley
line1: American illustrator and graphic designer based in Massachusetts; dubbed the "Dean of American Designers" by the Saturday Evening Post.
line2: Known for pioneering American Art Nouveau posters, designing for The Chap-Book, and publishing the periodical Bradley: His Book.

name: James Stevenson
line1: American cartoonist and illustrator based in New York; contributed to The New Yorker for over five decades.
line2: Known for nearly 2,000 New Yorker cartoons and 79 covers, and the Caldecott Honor book When I Was Nine.

name: George Tscherny
line1: Hungarian-born American graphic designer based in New York; former president of AIGA from 1966 to 1968.
line2: Known for corporate identity work for the Ford Foundation and Herman Miller, and the School of Visual Arts' flower logo.

name: R.J. Palacio
line1: American author and graphic designer based in New York; spent two decades designing book jackets before writing fiction.
line2: Known for her bestselling novel Wonder, its 2017 film adaptation, and cover designs for authors like Paul Auster.

name: Giovanni Pintori
line1: Italian graphic designer based in Milan; head of Olivetti's graphic design department from 1950 to 1967.
line2: Known for Olivetti's geometric advertising campaigns, typewriter posters, and the company's acclaimed annual calendars.

name: Tom Geismar
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; co-founder of the design firm Chermayeff & Geismar.
line2: Known for the Mobil, NBC, and Chase logos, the PBS "three-headed" mark, and U.S. transportation sign standards.

name: Edward Wright
line1: British typographer and graphic designer based in London; taught at the Central School of Arts and Crafts.
line2: Known for the rotating chrome sign at New Scotland Yard, Churchill College's foundation lettering, and the First Things First manifesto.

name: Buddy Esquire
line1: American graphic designer based in the Bronx; self-taught flyer artist dubbed "The Flyer King" of early hip-hop.
line2: Known for roughly 300 hand-drawn party flyers for Grandmaster Flash, Afrika Bambaataa, and the Cold Crush Brothers.

name: José Carlos de Brito e Cunha
line1: Brazilian cartoonist and graphic designer based in Rio de Janeiro; a leading illustrator of Brazil's early 20th-century press.
line2: Known as J. Carlos for his cover art for Para Todos magazine, work for O Malho, and shaping Brazil's Art Deco graphic style.

name: Michael Doret
line1: American lettering artist and logo designer based in New York; a Cooper Union graduate who trained under Ed Benguiat.
line2: Known for the New York Knicks logo, KISS album art, and decades of hand-lettered Time magazine covers.

name: László Moholy-Nagy
line1: Hungarian-born painter and photographer based in Chicago; former Bauhaus professor and founder of the New Bauhaus.
line2: Known for pioneering photograms, photomontage, and the "New Vision" approach to experimental photography.

name: Steve Martino
line1: American animation director and designer based in Los Angeles; longtime art director at Blue Sky Studios.
line2: Known for directing Horton Hears a Who!, Ice Age: Continental Drift, and The Peanuts Movie.

name: George Bokhua
line1: Georgian logo designer and illustrator based in Tbilisi; more than fifteen years in brand identity design.
line2: Known for a minimalist, grid-based logo style, branding work for clients like Disney, and the book Principles of Logo Design.

name: Georges Huel
line1: Canadian graphic designer based in Montreal; trained at the École des arts graphiques.
line2: Known for designing the 1976 Montreal Olympics logo and graphics program, and earlier design work for Expo 67.

name: Alphonse Mucha
line1: Czech painter and illustrator based in Paris; leading figure of the Art Nouveau poster movement.
line2: Known for his posters for Sarah Bernhardt, including Gismonda and Médée, and decorative works like Chocolat Idéal.

name: Kamil Lhoták
line1: Czech painter and illustrator based in Prague; a founding member of the wartime Group 42.
line2: Known for paintings of balloons, airships, and early automobiles, and illustrations for more than 400 books.

name: George Grosz
line1: German-born painter and draughtsman based in Berlin and later New York; a founding figure of Berlin Dada.
line2: Known for biting Weimar-era caricatures, pioneering photomontage with John Heartfield, and leading the New Objectivity movement.

name: Rune Söderqvist
line1: Swedish graphic designer based in Stockholm; ran his own design studio from the 1970s onward.
line2: Known for creating ABBA's backwards-B logo and designing the band's album sleeves from Arrival through its later releases.

name: Kosh
line1: English art director and album designer based in Los Angeles; former in-house designer for Apple Records.
line2: Known for the Eagles' Hotel California cover and logo, and sleeve design for the Beatles' Abbey Road and Let It Be.

name: Charles Bigelow
line1: American type designer and historian based in California; a 1982 MacArthur Fellow.
line2: Known for co-creating the Lucida typeface family and Wingdings with Kris Holmes, and researching on-screen type legibility.

name: Barney Bubbles
line1: British graphic designer based in London; in-house art director for Stiff Records in the late 1970s.
line2: Known for Elvis Costello's Armed Forces and My Aim Is True sleeves, and Ian Dury's multi-sleeve Do It Yourself album.

name: Hans Donner
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Austrian-born graphic designer based in Rio de Janeiro; longtime head of TV Globo's graphics department in Brazil.
line2: Known for pioneering computer-generated title sequences for Jornal Nacional and Fantástico, and modernizing Brazilian television graphics.

name: Dora Hauth-Trachsler
line1: Zurich-born Swiss painter and graphic designer active in the early 1900s; trained in Munich before returning home to teach and design posters.
line2: Known for her Swiss federal-festival posters, temperance-campaign poster art, and illustrated school textbooks.

name: Prabda Yoon
line1: Bangkok-born Thai writer, graphic designer, and filmmaker; studied at Parsons and Cooper Union in New York before returning to Thailand.
line2: Known for his S.E.A. Write Award-winning fiction, book design for Typhoon Studio, and directing the film Motel Mist.

name: Uli Huber
line1: German graphic designer and letterer (1902-1981) who spent his career in Berlin working across posters, packaging, and advertising.
line2: Known for his calligraphic lettering and logo design, his book Werbung + Graphik, and decades teaching at Berlin's State Graphics Institute.

name: Charley Harper
line1: West Virginia-born American illustrator and printmaker based in Cincinnati, pioneer of a geometric wildlife style he called minimal realism.
line2: Known for his Ford Times nature illustrations, Giant Golden Book of Biology artwork, and National Park Service posters.

name: Martin Lambie-Nairn
line1: British designer (1945-2020) based in London, pioneer of television branding who spent 12 years as consultant creative director at the BBC.
line2: Known for Channel 4's 1982 blocks logo, BBC Two's 1991 identity, and the BBC One globe idents of the late 1990s.

name: Stefan Sagmeister
line1: Austrian-born graphic designer based in New York, founder of Sagmeister & Walsh and a two-time Grammy winner for album packaging.
line2: Known for his Rolling Stones and Lou Reed album art, the self-lacerated AIGA lecture poster, and Things I Have Learned in My Life So Far.

name: James Pilditch
line1: British designer and consultant, founder of Package Design Associates, which grew into the corporate identity firm Allied International Designers.
line2: Known for pioneering corporate identity consulting in Britain, his book Communication by Design, and decades of packaging design leadership.

name: Robert Brownjohn
line1: American-born graphic designer who relocated to London and became known for inventive title sequences in British advertising and film.
line2: Known for the Goldfinger and From Russia with Love title sequences, and his Sex and Typography lecture on design and desire.

name: Koichi Sato
line1: Japanese graphic designer from Gunma Prefecture who left Shiseido's art department in 1971 to go freelance, later teaching at Tama Art University.
line2: Known for his Super-Oriental poster style blending classical Japanese motifs with modern color, including his landmark New Music Media poster.

name: Hiroshi Ohchi
line1: Japanese graphic designer and art director (1908-1974), a founding figure of Japan's postwar advertising design community.
line2: Known for serving as IDEA magazine's first art director, designing the Idemitsu Kosan logo, and leading AGI's Japanese chapter.

name: Jim Lee
line1: Korean-born American comic book artist and publisher, longtime Chief Creative Officer and Publisher at DC Comics.
line2: Known for illustrating the best-selling X-Men #1, co-founding Image Comics and WildStorm, and drawing Batman: Hush.

name: Kenny Gravillis
line1: American graphic designer based in Los Angeles, co-founder of Gravillis Inc. after starting his career in the Def Jam Records art department.
line2: Known for album art for Public Enemy and Notorious B.I.G., and movie posters for Straight Outta Compton and Bohemian Rhapsody.

name: Ursula Suess
line1: American graphic designer and letterer, raised in Munich before returning to New York to design book jackets for major publishers.
line2: Known for hand-lettering dozens of book jackets, her Book Jacket italic typeface, and teaching calligraphy at Cooper Union.

name: Gary Larson
line1: American cartoonist from Tacoma, Washington, who spent fifteen years drawing one of the most widely syndicated comic panels in the world.
line2: Known for creating The Far Side, his surreal single-panel cartoons syndicated in over 1,900 newspapers, and the book There's a Hair in My Dirt.

name: Paul Rand
line1: American graphic designer based in New York, a pioneer of modernist advertising art and longtime professor at Yale.
line2: Known for designing the IBM, UPS, ABC, and Westinghouse corporate logos, and his influential book Thoughts on Design.

name: Ivan Bilibin
line1: Russian illustrator and stage designer celebrated for his intricate illustrations of Russian fairy tales in the Art Nouveau style.
line2: Known for illustrating Vasilisa the Beautiful and other Russian folk tales, and designing sets for operas including The Golden Cockerel.

name: Carlos Cruz-Diez
line1: Venezuelan-born kinetic artist who spent most of his career based in Paris, a leading figure of 20th-century Op and kinetic art.
line2: Known for his Physichromie series, immersive Chromosaturation color installations, and Additive Color works exploring perception.

name: Seymour Chwast
line1: American illustrator and graphic designer based in New York, co-founder of the influential Pushpin Studios.
line2: Known for his eclectic poster and book illustration, the End War poster, and decades of Push Pin Graphic publications.

name: Amanda Jane Jones
line1: American graphic designer and illustrator who became the founding designer of Kinfolk magazine before going freelance.
line2: Known for shaping Kinfolk's minimalist visual identity, illustrated children's books like Yum Yummy Yuck, and collaborations with Opinel.

name: Alex Diggelmann
line1: Swiss graphic designer and poster artist (1902-1987) based in Zurich, one of the most celebrated Swiss commercial artists of his generation.
line2: Known for winning Olympic art-competition medals for his sports posters, designing tourism posters for Arosa and Gstaad, and the UEFA Cup trophy.

name: Bruno Monguzzi
line1: Swiss graphic designer from Ticino, trained in Geneva and London before working at Milan's Studio Boggeri and in Montreal.
line2: Known for the signage and visual identity of the Musee d'Orsay in Paris, Expo 67 pavilion graphics, and the USI university logo.

name: Jonathan Hoefler
line1: American type designer based in New York, co-founder of the Hoefler&Co type foundry.
line2: Known for designing Hoefler Text, co-creating Gotham, and the Chronicle and Sentinel typeface families.

name: Dick Bruna
line1: Dutch illustrator and author based in Utrecht, known for his flat, minimalist style using a limited bold color palette.
line2: Known for creating Miffy the rabbit, illustrating over 30 Miffy picture books, and designing iconic paperback covers for A.W. Bruna Uitgevers.

name: Willy Pogany
line1: Hungarian-born illustrator who emigrated to the United States and became a leading book illustrator of the early 20th century.
line2: Known for his lavish illustrations for Parsifal and The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, and later work as a Hollywood art director.

name: Tim Burton
line1: American filmmaker and illustrator from Burbank, California, who began his career as an animator at Walt Disney Studios.
line2: Known for directing Edward Scissorhands and The Nightmare Before Christmas, and his gothic illustrated book The Melancholy Death of Oyster Boy.

name: Morteza Momayez
line1: Iranian graphic designer and educator based in Tehran, widely regarded as the father of modern Iranian graphic design.
line2: Known for his film and theater posters, founding the Iranian Graphic Design Society, and receiving Icograda's Lifetime Achievement Award.

name: Ismar David
line1: Breslau-born calligrapher and type designer who worked in Jerusalem before settling in New York as a book designer and teacher.
line2: Known for creating David Hebrew, the first comprehensive Hebrew typeface family, and teaching calligraphy at Cooper Union and Pratt Institute.

name: Tobias Frere-Jones
line1: American type designer based in New York, formerly a partner at the Hoefler & Frere-Jones type foundry.
line2: Known for designing the Interstate, Gotham, and Poynter typeface families used worldwide in signage and branding.

name: Michael Bierut
line1: American graphic designer based in New York, a partner at Pentagram since 1990 after beginning his career at Vignelli Associates.
line2: Known for identity work for Saks Fifth Avenue and MIT Media Lab, his Design Observer writing, and the book 79 Short Essays on Design.

name: Alois Carigiet
line1: Graubunden-born Swiss painter, graphic designer, and stage designer who co-founded the satirical Cabaret Cornichon in Zurich.
line2: Known for illustrating the children's classic Schellen-Ursli, and winning the Hans Christian Andersen Award for illustration in 1966.

name: Shag
line1: American pop-surrealist painter, born Josh Agle, based in Southern California and known professionally as Shag.
line2: Known for his retro cocktail-culture paintings of mid-century lounge life, Disneyland art collaborations, and the Shagland gallery/boutique.

name: Gaspar Saladino
line1: American comic-book letterer and logo designer based in New York; worked for DC Comics across five decades from the Silver Age onward.
line2: Known for designing the Swamp Thing and Vertigo logos, and hand-lettering classic Batman and Green Lantern stories.

name: Tomoko Miho
line1: Japanese-American graphic designer based in New York; former senior designer at CBS and a principal at Unimark International.
line2: Known for corporate identity and publication design for CBS, IBM, and Knoll, and exhibition design for the Smithsonian Institution.

name: Hildreth Meière
line1: American Art Deco muralist and designer based in New York; first woman appointed to the New York City Art Commission.
line2: Known for the enamel-and-metal roundels on Radio City Music Hall's facade, and murals at St. Bartholomew's Church and the Nebraska Capitol.

name: Alexander Liberman
line1: Russian-born American artist and editor based in New York; longtime editorial director of Condé Nast Publications, including Vogue.
line2: Known for shaping Vogue's visual identity for decades, large-scale welded steel sculpture, and abstract painting.

name: Bob Cato
line1: American graphic designer and art director based in New York; vice president of creative services at Columbia Records.
line2: Known for album covers for Bob Dylan, Barbra Streisand, and Big Brother and the Holding Company's Cheap Thrills.

name: Mitsuo Katsui
line1: Japanese graphic designer based in Tokyo; art director for the 1970 Osaka Expo and emeritus professor at Musashino Art University.
line2: Known for bold experimental posters blending Japanese and Latin type, and pioneering work in digital graphic design.

name: Erik Nitsche
line1: Swiss-born graphic designer based in New York; art director for General Dynamics during the Cold War atomic age.
line2: Known for his abstract 'Atoms for Peace' poster series, General Dynamics annual reports, and the book Dynamic America.

name: David Carson
line1: American graphic designer based in California; former art director of Ray Gun magazine and pioneer of 1990s grunge typography.
line2: Known for deconstructed layouts in Ray Gun, Beach Culture, and Surfer magazine, and the bestselling book The End of Print.

name: Sol LeWitt
line1: American conceptual artist based in New York and Connecticut; a founding figure of Minimalism and Conceptual art.
line2: Known for instruction-based wall drawings, cube and grid sculptures, and his 1967 essay Paragraphs on Conceptual Art.

name: Marget Aagot Larsen
line1: American graphic designer and art director based in San Francisco; art director for the department store Joseph Magnin.
line2: Known for a distinctive, Paul Klee-influenced advertising style that helped define 1950s-60s American retail design.

name: Leif Frimann Anisdahl
line1: Norwegian graphic designer and typographer based in Drammen; a pioneer of professional graphic design in Norway from the 1960s.
line2: Known for corporate identities for Norsk Hydro, Storebrand, and Posten, and the 'Norway alphabet' for the Foreign Ministry.

name: Chip Kidd
line1: American graphic designer based in New York; longtime associate art director at Alfred A. Knopf.
line2: Known for the Jurassic Park logo, hundreds of acclaimed book jacket designs, and writing on design and comics.

name: Richard Paul Lohse
line1: Swiss concrete artist and graphic designer based in Zurich; a key figure of Swiss Style typography and Concrete Art.
line2: Known for serial, modular abstract paintings, Swiss Style poster design, and co-founding the journal Neue Grafik.

name: Charles Dana Gibson
line1: American illustrator based in New York; owner and editor of the humor magazine Life in the early 20th century.
line2: Known for creating the iconic 'Gibson Girl,' pen-and-ink illustrations for Collier's and Harper's, and social satire.

name: Helen Federico
line1: American graphic designer, painter, and illustrator based in New York; former associate art director under Paul Rand.
line2: Known for illustrated children's and cookbooks, and advertising and editorial work for IBM, Doubleday, and Fortune.

name: Yumeji Takehisa
line1: Japanese painter, poet, and graphic designer active in the Taisho era; a largely self-taught, widely popular artist.
line2: Known as the symbol of 'Taisho romanticism' for lyrical bijin-ga paintings, book design, and kimono-textile patterns.

name: Daphne van Peski
line1: Dutch graphic designer based in Amsterdam; longtime designer at the influential firm Total Design alongside Wim Crouwel.
line2: Known for Stedelijk Museum and Fodor exhibition catalogues, and book design including Heart Beat (2006).

name: Gerry Barney
line1: British graphic designer based in London; worked at the Design Research Unit before co-founding Sedley Place in 1978.
line2: Known for designing the British Rail 'double arrow' logo in 1965, one of the UK's most enduring corporate symbols.

name: Hiroshi Yoshida
line1: Japanese woodblock print artist and painter active in the early 20th century; a leading figure of the shin-hanga movement.
line2: Known for landscape print series depicting Japan, the US, and Europe, including views of Mt. Fuji and the Grand Canyon.

name: Bernard Villemot
line1: French poster artist based in Paris; one of the last great names of 20th-century French commercial poster design.
line2: Known for iconic advertising posters for Perrier, Air France, and Bally shoes, rendered in bold flat color.

name: Chuck Jones
line1: American animator and director based in Hollywood; longtime director at Warner Bros.' Looney Tunes studio.
line2: Known for directing Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and Road Runner cartoons, and creating How the Grinch Stole Christmas (1966).

name: Maurice Neumont
line1: French lithographer and poster artist based in Paris; a leading figure of the WWI-era 'Patriotic School' of propaganda art.
line2: Known for the WWI poster On ne passe pas!, decades of illustrated menus for the Cornet Society, and founding the Salon des Humoristes.

name: Josef Váchal
line1: Czech printmaker, writer, and book artist based in Bohemia; a singular figure outside any established art movement.
line2: Known for thousands of hand-colored woodcuts, mystically themed handmade books, and the Portmoneum house in Litomyšl.

name: Frank Newbould
line1: British poster artist based in London; a leading designer for the London & North Eastern Railway between the world wars.
line2: Known for evocative railway travel posters and the WWII 'Your Britain - Fight for It Now' countryside campaign.

name: Mark Rothko
line1: Latvian-born American painter based in New York; a leading figure of Abstract Expressionism and color field painting.
line2: Known for luminous, large-scale color field canvases and the murals created for the Rothko Chapel in Houston.

name: Vincent Connare
line1: American typeface designer based in the United Kingdom; former type designer at Microsoft in the 1990s.
line2: Known for designing the Comic Sans and Trebuchet MS typefaces, now among the most widely used fonts in the world.

name: Alan Fletcher
line1: British graphic designer based in London; co-founder of the design consultancy Pentagram.
line2: Known for the V&A Museum's ampersand logo, corporate identity for Reuters, and his book The Art of Looking Sideways.

name: Warja Lavater
line1: Swiss artist and illustrator based in Paris; a pioneer of the modern wordless artist's book.
line2: Known for accordion-fold 'Imageries' retelling fairy tales like Little Red Riding Hood and Snow White entirely in symbols.

name: Théo Ballmer
line1: Swiss graphic designer based in Basel; an early pioneer of grid-based typography that shaped the Swiss Style.
line2: Known for his 1928 'Büro' poster series and modular grid layouts that influenced International Typographic Style.

name: Tom Eckersley
line1: British poster designer based in London; longtime head of design at the London College of Printing.
line2: Known for witty, minimal posters for London Transport, the GPO, and wartime public information campaigns.

name: Marianne Brandt
line1: German Bauhaus-trained designer and photographer; led the Bauhaus metal workshop in Dessau in the late 1920s.
line2: Known for her modernist tea infusers and ashtrays, the Kandem bedside lamp, and experimental self-portrait photomontages.

name: Alfred Roller
line1: Austrian graphic and stage designer based in Vienna; co-founder and president of the Vienna Secession.
line2: Known for Ver Sacrum cover designs and Secession exhibition posters, and his stage designs with Gustav Mahler at the Vienna Court Opera.

name: Dóra Keresztes
line1: Hungarian illustrator and graphic designer based in Budapest; vice president of the Society of Hungarian Illustrators.
line2: Known for children's book illustration, Hungarian film and theatre poster design, and the animated short Moon Film.

name: György Kepes
line1: Hungarian-born artist and designer who taught visual design at MIT after emigrating to the U.S. in 1937.
line2: Known for founding MIT's Center for Advanced Visual Studies and writing the influential book The Language of Vision.

name: Carson Ellis
line1: Canadian-born American illustrator based in Portland, Oregon; longtime album artist for the band The Decemberists.
line2: Known for illustrating The Mysterious Benedict Society, her Caldecott Honor book Du Iz Tak?, and The Decemberists' album art.

name: Paula Scher
line1: American graphic designer and painter based in New York; partner at Pentagram since 1991.
line2: Known for her identity and poster designs for The Public Theater, Citibank, and Tiffany & Co.

name: Charles R. Chickering
line1: American illustrator who became a U.S. postage stamp designer at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing from 1947.
line2: Known for designing roughly 77 U.S. stamps, including the 1962 Project Mercury issue, after years as a magazine illustrator.

name: Clemente Padín
line1: Uruguayan graphic designer and mail artist based in Montevideo; imprisoned in the late 1970s for his political art.
line2: Known for pioneering Latin American mail art, organizing the Creative Postcard Festival, and editing the magazine OVUM 10.

name: Peter Saville
line1: English graphic designer and art director based in London; co-founder and art director of Factory Records in Manchester.
line2: Known for album covers for Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures and New Order's Blue Monday, and the Haçienda nightclub branding.

name: Ira Schnapp
line1: Austro-Hungarian-born American letterer and logo designer; longtime in-house staff artist at DC Comics from the 1940s through the 1960s.
line2: Known for designing the Superman and Batman logos, DC's signature cover lettering, and decades of the company's house ads.

name: Joe Simon
line1: American comic book writer and artist based in New York; first editor-in-chief of Timely Comics, the predecessor to Marvel.
line2: Known for co-creating Captain America with Jack Kirby, pioneering the romance comics genre, and founding Sick magazine.

name: Katherine McCoy
line1: American graphic designer and educator based in Michigan; co-chaired Cranbrook Academy of Art's graduate design program for over two decades.
line2: Known for shaping postmodern graphic design pedagogy at Cranbrook, co-founding the High Ground design conference, and winning the AIGA Medal.

name: Robert Ingpen
line1: Australian illustrator and author based in Melbourne; first Australian to win the Hans Christian Andersen Award for illustration, in 1986.
line2: Known for illustrated editions of Treasure Island and Peter Pan, and the Encyclopedia of Things That Never Were.

name: Titus Yocarini
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Indonesian illustrator and graphic designer working in a bold, lettering-driven commercial style.
line2: Known for editorial and poster illustration work and hand-lettered typographic design.

name: Aaron Draplin
line1: American graphic designer based in Portland, Oregon; founder of Draplin Design Co. (DDC).
