line2: Known for Field Notes notebook branding, bold Rust Belt-inspired logo and poster design, and the book Pretty Much Everything.

name: Robert Bringhurst
line1: Canadian poet, typographer, and translator based in British Columbia; trained in classical typesetting and book design.
line2: Known for writing The Elements of Typographic Style, translating Haida oral literature, and co-authoring The Raven Steals the Light.

name: Johan De Moor
line1: Belgian comic artist based in Brussels; son of Tintin collaborator Bob De Moor.
line2: Known for continuing the comic strip Cubitus after creator Dupa's death, and co-creating the series Le Moine fou.

name: Colin Thompson
line1: British-born illustrator and author based in Australia; known for richly detailed, surreal picture-book art.
line2: Known for The Paperbag Prince, How to Live Forever, and the Floods fantasy novel series.

name: Pierre Alechinsky
line1: Belgian painter and printmaker based in Paris; founding member of the CoBrA art movement.
line2: Known for gestural calligraphic abstraction, comic-strip-like marginal panels, and acrylic-on-paper technique.

name: Arthur Eisenmenger
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] German graphic designer; former chief graphic designer of the European Economic Community.
line2: Known for designing the euro currency symbol (€), based on the Greek letter epsilon.

name: Mary Blair
line1: American visual artist and animator; influential color stylist at Walt Disney Studios in the 1940s-50s.
line2: Known for concept art on Cinderella, Alice in Wonderland, and Peter Pan, and designing It's a Small World.

name: Edmund Dulac
line1: French-born illustrator naturalized as a British citizen; leading figure of the golden age of illustration.
line2: Known for lavish fairy-tale illustrations for The Arabian Nights and Hans Christian Andersen, and British banknote design.

name: Eric Shanower
line1: American comic book writer and artist based in California; multiple Eisner Award winner.
line2: Known for the historical epic Age of Bronze, his adaptations of L. Frank Baum's Oz books, and Little Nemo: Return to Slumberland.

name: Bruno Munari
line1: Italian artist and designer based in Milan; started in the Futurist movement before shaping postwar Italian design.
line2: Known for his Useless Machines sculptures, innovative children's books, and industrial design for Danese.

name: Hans Hillmann
line1: German graphic designer and illustrator based in Kassel; a leading figure in postwar German film poster design.
line2: Known for minimalist posters for the Neue Filmkunst distributor and New German Cinema, and comic adaptations of The Trial and Moby-Dick.

name: Joža Uprka
line1: Czech (Moravian) painter and graphic artist active around 1900; a leading figure of Art Nouveau in Moravia.
line2: Known for vivid paintings of Moravian Slovácko folk life and costume, including Ride of the Kings, and close ties to Alphonse Mucha's circle.

name: Ed Benguiat
line1: American type designer and lettering artist based in New York; longtime creative force at Photo-Lettering Inc. and ITC.
line2: Known for the ITC Benguiat and Tiffany typefaces, and logos for Planet of the Apes, The A-Team, and Esquire magazine.

name: Jon Hicks
line1: British graphic and icon designer based in the UK; founder of the design studio Hicksdesign.
line2: Known for designing the Firefox browser logo, the Skype icon, and the original CSS3 shield badge.

name: Berthold Wolpe
line1: German-born British typographer and book designer based in London; taught at the Central School of Art and Design.
line2: Known for designing the Albertus typeface, decades of Faber & Faber book jacket designs, and the Fanfare and Sachsenwald typefaces.

name: Donald Brun
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Swiss graphic designer and poster artist based in Basel, active from the 1930s through the 1960s.
line2: Known for bold, witty advertising posters for Swiss brands, part of the mid-20th-century Basel school of poster art alongside Herbert Leupin.

name: James Broom Lynne
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] British graphic designer and illustrator active in London from the 1950s to the 1970s.
line2: Known for modernist book jacket designs for Penguin and Pelican Books, and work as a design tutor at the Central School of Art and Design.

name: Yuko Shimizu
line1: Japanese-born illustrator based in New York City; longtime faculty member at the School of Visual Arts.
line2: Known for her covers for Vertigo's The Unwritten, editorial art for The New York Times and TIME, and multiple Society of Illustrators medals.

name: Steve Ditko
line1: American comic book artist and writer based in New York City; co-creator at Marvel Comics in the 1960s.
line2: Known for co-creating Spider-Man and Doctor Strange, and for later creating the Question and Mr. A.

name: Heinrich Campendonk
line1: German-born painter and stained-glass artist who later became a naturalized Dutch citizen; youngest member of Der Blaue Reiter.
line2: Known for his Expressionist paintings alongside Franz Marc and Kandinsky, stained-glass windows, and later teaching in Amsterdam.

name: Sheila Levrant de Bretteville
line1: American graphic designer and educator based in Los Angeles and New Haven; first woman tenured at Yale School of Art.
line2: Known for co-founding the Woman's Building in L.A., chairing Yale's graphic design program, and the public artwork Biddy Mason: Time and Place.

name: Ron van Roon
line1: Dutch graphic designer based in the Netherlands; ran his own Amsterdam studio, later Rouwhorst + Van Roon, for five decades.
line2: Known for posters, logos, and book covers for clients including VPRO, NOS, Nijgh & Van Ditmar, and Triodos Bank.

name: Raymond Savignac
line1: French poster artist based in Paris; trained under A.M. Cassandre before becoming a leading 20th-century poster designer.
line2: Known for his 1949 Monsavon soap poster, humorous ad campaigns for Air France and Cinzano, and the 1951 Grand Prix de l'Affiche.

name: O'Plérou Grebet
line1: Ivorian graphic designer and illustrator based in Abidjan; began a yearlong emoji-a-day project in 2018 called Zouzoukwa.
line2: Known for his Zouzoukwa emoji celebrating West African culture, designing UNHCR's World Refugee Day emoji, and proposing new Unicode symbols.

name: Hermann Zapf
line1: German type designer and calligrapher based in Darmstadt; worked across the hot-metal, phototype, and digital typesetting eras.
line2: Known for designing the typefaces Palatino, Optima, and Zapfino.

name: Ladislav Sutnar
line1: Czech-born graphic designer based in New York; pioneer of information design and former director of Prague's State School of Graphic Arts.
line2: Known for his information design at Sweet's Catalog Service, popularizing parentheses around phone area codes, and the book Visual Design in Action.

name: Théophile Steinlen
line1: Swiss-born illustrator and poster designer naturalized French in 1901; central figure of Montmartre's Chat Noir cabaret scene.
line2: Known for his iconic Chat Noir poster, cover illustrations for Gil Blas Illustré, and socially engaged Belle Époque lithographs.

name: Johannes Itten
line1: Swiss painter and theorist who taught the foundational preliminary course (Vorkurs) at the Bauhaus in Weimar during the 1920s.
line2: Known for pioneering color theory, the twelve-hue color wheel and seven contrasts of color, and his book The Art of Color.

name: Mac Conner
line1: American commercial illustrator based in New York; a leading mid-century "Mad Men"-era figure in magazine and advertising art.
line2: Known for illustrations in The Saturday Evening Post and Ladies' Home Journal, and ad campaigns for United Airlines and General Motors.

name: Rob Schröder
line1: Dutch graphic designer and filmmaker based in Amsterdam; co-founder of the politically engaged design collective Wild Plakken.
line2: Known for anti-apartheid protest posters, teaching at the Gerrit Rietveld Academie, and later documentary filmmaking for VPRO.

name: Louis Christiaan Kalff
line1: Dutch designer and architect; longtime art director at Philips from the mid-1920s through the 1950s.
line2: Known for designing the Philips logo, the Evoluon building in Eindhoven, and the 1958 Philips Pavilion with Le Corbusier.

name: Albe Steiner
line1: Italian graphic designer and former WWII partisan based in Milan; art director at La Rinascente in the early 1950s.
line2: Known for the original Coop supermarket logo, book design for Feltrinelli and Zanichelli, and co-founding Italy's ADI design association.

name: Alexander Isley
line1: American graphic designer based in Redding, Connecticut; the first full-time art director of Spy magazine in the 1980s.
line2: Known for founding Alexander Isley Inc., branding and packaging work held in MoMA's permanent collection, and the 2014 AIGA Medal.

name: Louis Danziger
line1: New York-born graphic designer who built his influential practice in Los Angeles starting in 1949.
line2: Known for identity and advertising work for the Container Corporation of America and LACMA, and the 1998 AIGA Medal.

name: Gert Wunderlich
line1: German typographer and book designer based in Leipzig; longtime professor at the Hochschule für Grafik und Buchkunst.
line2: Known for designing the Maxima sans-serif typeface family, widely used in East Germany, and the Leipzig Gutenberg Prize.

name: Okuda San Miguel
line1: Spanish street artist and muralist based in Madrid, working under the name Okuda San Miguel.
line2: Known for the Kaos Temple skate park mural in Spain, large-scale geometric murals worldwide, and colorful pop-surrealist sculpture.

name: Corita Kent
line1: American pop artist and former Catholic nun known as Sister Mary Corita; taught art at Immaculate Heart College in Los Angeles.
line2: Known for bold serigraph prints with social justice messages, the 1985 U.S. Postal Service LOVE stamp, and Boston's rainbow gas tank mural.

name: Wim Crouwel
line1: Dutch graphic designer and typographer based in Amsterdam; co-founder of the influential design firm Total Design.
line2: Known for the grid-based New Alphabet typeface, posters and catalogs for the Stedelijk Museum, and Dutch postage stamp designs.

name: Marjane Satrapi
line1: Iranian-born graphic novelist, illustrator, and filmmaker based in Paris, France.
line2: Known for the autobiographical graphic novel Persepolis, its Oscar-nominated animated film adaptation, and Chicken with Plums.

name: El Lissitzky
line1: Russian artist and graphic designer, a leading figure of early 20th-century Constructivism and Suprematism.
line2: Known for the propaganda poster Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge, his Proun series, and pioneering modernist typography and exhibition design.

name: Chris Reccardi
line1: American animation artist and designer based in Los Angeles; longtime collaborator of John Kricfalusi at Spumco.
line2: Known for background art and design on The Ren & Stimpy Show, and later directing and design work for Cartoon Network and Nickelodeon.

name: Romek Marber
line1: Polish-born graphic designer based in London; fled to Britain as a refugee after surviving World War II.
line2: Known for creating the influential "Marber Grid" cover template used on Penguin Books' crime and fiction series in the 1960s.

name: Shusei Nagaoka
line1: Japanese illustrator and airbrush artist based in Tokyo, active from the 1970s through the 1990s.
line2: Known for airbrushed album art for Earth, Wind & Fire including I Am and Faces, and key visual art for the Mobile Suit Gundam anime franchise.

name: Fideli Sundqvist
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Finnish illustrator and graphic designer based in Helsinki, known for playful, flat-color editorial illustration.
line2: Known for whimsical illustrations for international magazines, advertising campaigns, and children's book projects.

name: İhap Hulusi Görey
line1: Turkish graphic designer and poster artist active in Istanbul from the 1920s to the 1960s; a pioneer of modern Turkish graphic design.
line2: Known for iconic advertising posters for Turkish cigarette brands, wartime propaganda posters, and early Turkish corporate branding work.

name: Leslie Ragan
line1: American illustrator and painter active in New York during the 1930s and 1940s, known for his Art Deco style.
line2: Known for iconic travel posters for the New York Central Railroad, including the 20th Century Limited, and streamlined views of American cities.

name: Alfred Pal
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Croatian cartoonist and illustrator based in Zagreb, active across much of the 20th century.
line2: Known for satirical cartoons in Kerempuh magazine and drawings documenting his imprisonment at the Jasenovac concentration camp.

name: Dorothy E. Hayes
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] American color consultant and designer active in the postwar era; a pioneering voice in color forecasting for industry.
line2: Known for advising manufacturers on color trends, consulting on package and product color schemes, and shaping the color-forecasting profession.

name: Herbert Thannhaeuser
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] German type designer active in Dresden in the early twentieth century, working in the geometric sans-serif New Typography tradition.
line2: Known for designing the geometric sans-serif typeface Element, produced for the Schriftguss AG Dresden type foundry.

name: Pino Tovaglia
line1: Italian graphic designer based in Milan; a leading figure of the postwar Studio Boggeri circle and member of Alliance Graphique Internationale.
line2: Known for the identity and signage system for the Milan Metro, corporate design for La Rinascente, and rational Swiss-influenced visual systems.

name: Richard Amsel
line1: American illustrator based in New York; one of the most sought-after movie poster artists of the 1970s and 1980s.
line2: Known for the posters for Raiders of the Lost Ark, The Sting, and Flash Gordon, plus numerous Rolling Stone covers.

name: Barbara Stauffacher Solomon
line1: American graphic designer and artist trained at the Basel School of Design; later practiced as a landscape architect in California.
line2: Known for pioneering bold 'supergraphics' murals at the Sea Ranch Athletic Club, blending Swiss design discipline with American pop scale.

name: Hans Hartmann
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Swiss graphic designer active in the mid-twentieth century, working within the Swiss International Style design tradition.
line2: Known for poster and corporate design work produced in Switzerland's postwar design scene, among its Basel- and Zurich-trained designers.

name: Stuart Davis
line1: American painter based in New York; a pioneering modernist who bridged Cubism and an emerging American pop sensibility.
line2: Known for the paintings Lucky Strike, Swing Landscape, and Visa, which fused commercial lettering and jazz rhythm into fine art.

name: Ernst Roch
line1: Czech-born graphic designer based in Montreal; co-founder of the influential design firm Gottschalk+Ash International.
line2: Known for signage and graphics for Expo 67, Canadian corporate identity programs, and stamp designs for Canada Post.

name: Dick Elffers
line1: Dutch graphic designer based in Rotterdam; a leading figure in postwar Dutch exhibition and poster design.
line2: Known for posters and displays for the De Bijenkorf department store, exhibition design, and large-scale public tapestries and murals.

name: Louis Lozowick
line1: Ukrainian-born American painter and printmaker based in New York; a central figure of the Precisionist movement.
line2: Known for machine-age lithographs of American skylines and bridges, including his New York series celebrating industrial modernity.

name: Gerd Arntz
line1: German-born printmaker based in the Netherlands; creator of the visual language behind Otto Neurath's Isotype system.
line2: Known for designing thousands of simplified pictograms used in the Vienna Method of picture statistics, and for his woodcut prints.

name: Fred Troller
line1: Swiss-born graphic designer based in New York; trained in Zurich and shaped by Geigy's pioneering in-house design studio before emigrating.
line2: Known for corporate identity and poster design for Geigy in Switzerland, and decades of identity and exhibition design work in New York.

name: Karel Teige
line1: Czech avant-garde typographer and critic based in Prague; leading theorist of the Devětsil group between the world wars.
line2: Known for radical typography and book covers for Czech poetist literature, photomontage work, and influential writings on modern architecture.

name: Edward McKnight Kauffer
line1: American-born poster artist based in London; one of the most influential commercial artists of the early twentieth century.
line2: Known for his posters for the London Underground, advertising work for Shell, and bold modernist eagle and dove motifs.

name: Rolf Müller
line1: German graphic designer based in Munich; part of the design team behind the visual identity of the 1972 Munich Olympics.
line2: Known for Olympic signage and pictograms, founding his own Büro Rolf Müller studio, and corporate design for German clients.

name: Wassily Kandinsky
line1: Russian-born painter based in Germany and later Paris; a founding pioneer of abstract art and Bauhaus faculty member.
line2: Known for the Composition series, his role in the Blue Rider circle, and the theoretical writings Concerning the Spiritual in Art.

name: Lucille Tenazas
line1: Filipino-American graphic designer based in San Francisco and later New York; chaired the MFA Design program at Parsons.
line2: Known for narrative-driven identity and book design through her studio Tenazas Design, and receiving the AIGA Medal in 2015.

name: Paul Klee
line1: Swiss-German painter based in Munich and later Switzerland; a key Bauhaus faculty member alongside Kandinsky.
line2: Known for paintings including Twittering Machine and Senecio, and his influential Bauhaus teaching notes on color and form.

name: Wally Olins
line1: British branding consultant based in London; co-founder of Wolff Olins and later founder of Saffron Brand Consultants.
line2: Known for rebranding Orange and Renault, shaping corporate identity practice worldwide, and writing On Brand and Corporate Identity.

name: Herbert Leupin
line1: Swiss poster artist based in Basel; a master of the mid-century 'Sachplakat' object poster style.
line2: Known for advertising posters for PKZ menswear, Erdal shoe polish, and Camel cigarettes.

name: Willy Fleckhaus
line1: German graphic designer based in Cologne; legendary art director known for radically reinventing magazine layout.
line2: Known for his photo-driven design of Twen magazine in the 1960s, and the colored spine system for Suhrkamp and Insel book covers.

name: Max Bill
line1: Swiss artist and designer based in Zurich; Bauhaus-trained co-founder and first rector of the Ulm School of Design.
line2: Known for his Concrete Art sculpture, the Junghans wristwatch designs, and the Ulmer Hocker stool.

name: Hans Bohn
line1: [LOW CONFIDENCE] Swiss graphic designer active in the mid-twentieth century, working within the Zurich school of modernist design.
line2: Known for poster and typographic design produced within Switzerland's postwar International Typographic Style movement.

name: Max Miedinger
line1: Swiss typeface designer based in Münchenstein; worked as a typesetter and sales representative for the Haas Type Foundry.
line2: Known for co-creating Neue Haas Grotesk with Eduard Hoffmann in 1957, later renamed Helvetica, one of the world's most used typefaces.

name: Paul Bacon
line1: American book jacket designer based in New York; pioneered the bold 'Big Book' paperback cover look of the 1960s.
line2: Known for the covers of Catch-22, Portnoy's Complaint, and The Exorcist, plus earlier jazz album art for Savoy Records.

name: Lemi Ghariokwu
line1: Nigerian illustrator based in Lagos; self-taught artist who became Afrobeat's defining album cover artist.
line2: Known for politically charged cover art for Fela Kuti's Zombie, Coffin for Head of State, and Shuffering and Shmiling.

name: Hermann-Paul
line1: French illustrator and printmaker based in Paris; a leading caricaturist of the fin-de-siècle satirical press.
line2: Known for political caricatures in Le Rire and L'Assiette au Beurre, and for prints made during the Dreyfus affair era.

name: Daniel Rueda
line1: Spanish photographer and architect based in Valencia; known for meticulously staged, color-coordinated travel photography.
line2: Known for the long-running Volumes project with Anna Devís, pairing geometric architecture with perfectly matched outfits worldwide.

name: Dave McKean
line1: British illustrator and filmmaker based in London; a defining visual artist of modern graphic novels.
line2: Known for his cover art for Neil Gaiman's The Sandman, the graphic novel Arkham Asylum, and directing the film MirrorMask.

name: Douglas Coupland
line1: Canadian novelist and visual artist based in Vancouver; trained at Emily Carr College of Art and Design.
line2: Known for coining 'Generation X' in his debut novel, and for public sculptures including Digital Orca in Vancouver.

name: Rafael Esquer
line1: Mexican-born graphic designer based in New York; founder and creative director of Alfalfa Studio after roles at Pentagram and Saatchi & Saatchi.
line2: Known for leading the restoration of Brooklyn's Masstransiscope subway art installation, and for branding and typographic design work.
